newsitem.title: USA: Rubin urges support for U.S. inner-city funding.
newsitem.headline: Rubin urges support for U.S. inner-city funding.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Wednesday urged Congress to back a program for promoting economic development in depressed inner-city areas, saying the problem has been ignored too long.

Testifying before the House appropriations subcommittee on Veterans Administration and Housing and Urban Development, he said the best vehicle for battling poverty in U.S. cities was the Community Development Financial Institutions Fund.
It aims to boost credit availability to poor urban, rural and Native American communities to boost economic development.
Rubin, seeking support for the administration's budget request for the fund, said it was important to all Americans to try to help inner-city residents better their lives.

"We lose tremendously in terms of economic potential and in a worsening of our social conditions because of these tremendous problems that have historically not been dealt with in this country," Rubin said.

Since the fund began in 1995, it has made a significant contribution to increasing access to private sector capital, he said. In January 1996, there were 268 applications under the program and 32 were subsequently selected to receive over $37 million in financial and technical assistance, he added.
